title: Agent-specific thinking settings bypass the mutually exclusive configuration contract
reasoning: Validation rejects simultaneous top-level thinking and max_thinking_tokens, but agent_specific dictionaries bypass that validation. get_thinking_config returns both values unchanged when an agent override specifies both, contradicting its explicit guarantee that at most one is set. Invalid preset values also bypass the declared ThinkingPreset return contract.
reproduction: Construct a ModelDefinition with agent_specific={'claude_code': {'thinking': 'high', 'max_thinking_tokens': 10000}}. Construction succeeds and get_thinking_config('claude_code') returns ('high', 10000).
recommendation: Validate the recognized thinking fields in each agent override using the same type and mutual-exclusion rules as the top-level configuration.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests reject conflicting top-level settings but only exercise individually valid agent-specific overrides.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand thinking configuration validation scenarios across top-level and agent-specific settings, checking conflicting pairs and invalid presets while preserving valid override precedence.
minimumFixScope: Extend ModelDefinition thinking validation and TestModelDefinitionThinking.
